title: Large personal Amiga/DOS behavioral and application recovery discovery
summary: Personally screen 686 candidate URLs and add 11 projects, with seven explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root assistant personally searched 20 GitHub query routes across Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS plus source-lineage follow-ups; screened 686 unique URLs and inspected 21 repositories. Eleven additions and seven explicit non-promotions; three additional inspected sources (tbx, LineWars II SDL and nitecrwl) were already tracked and left unchanged. Newly qualified additions are Amiga/DOS; no ST/CPC result was padded with forks or unrelated firmware. Distinguish behavioral ports, compiler-matching claims, partial function experiments, scientific runtime differences and modified gameplay. All claims remain source-reviewed rather than independently built; no upstream program, installer or compiler executed.

sources.reason: Native structured Rust game logic recovered from Amiga and Mac versions, including missions, driving and combat; inspected level state and address-linked source.
DOS 2.10 game transcribed from decompiled rules, AI and screens into Python/pygame. Inspected pathfinder preserves original address references and shared-RNG call-order dependency.
Experimental recovered C functions from MicroProse DOS executable. Actual samples include allocation and command dispatch with stub callees and placeholder strings, not a recovered whole game.

Address-linked native JavaScript parser, VGA drawing and original GAME.DAT script interpreter; original author directed binary/data reconstruction. The interpreter executes game scripts, not x86 instructions.
Substantive recovered setup script interpreter, graphics/UI and INI modules for the installer used by Blue Byte games such as Albion and Extreme Assault.

Recovered USNO astronomy application, with 74 application routines claimed and original FORTRAN runtime excluded. Inspected address-linked Chebyshev ephemeris reader contains native Fortran formulas and packed-coefficient handling.
Modern Rust platform layer around demech2 recovered native C/C++ game logic; inspected original AI weapon module contains typed functions rather than CPU instruction dispatch.

Native Rust port using JJFFE 2.8a7 gameplay reference and FFED3D rendering research. Inspected market formulas retain F619/F620 provenance and original-style RNG; model programs are game-data commands, not x86 execution.
Recovered WIZARDS.EXE and MAGIC.EXE sources plus interactive source map. Inspected combat/world-generation modules and build driver preserve overlay/link order and original-address provenance.
Native browser command RPG with executable-offset references and Borland RNG implementation. Reviewed gameplay and RNG sources, not merely a themed emulator wrapper.
Substantive enhanced continuation of wonst719/u5d decompiled engine with native combat modules, modern input/display/save systems and Workshop tooling.
Unrelated modern web-security toolkit. DOS search match is denial-of-service terminology, not a DOS historical application; no tool executed.
GitHub identifies this as a fork of already tracked theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste. Reviewed implementation/backlog but no independent continuation established; avoid duplicating the conversion.
GitHub identifies a fork of already tracked fredangstadt-lang/LineWarsII-DOS; no separate recovery promoted. SDL continuation is also already tracked.
Worms Armageddon Windows recovery, not original DOS Worms. Interesting native source work but outside the requested source-platform focus.
Original is a 16-bit Windows 3.x NE executable, not a DOS game. Native Linux decompilation is separately useful but outside this focused batch.
Main recovered engine is the 1997 Win32 ProVoice DLL; DOS voice conversions are supporting tooling, not a recovered original DOS speech engine. Preserve for a Windows/application pass.
Fork of drcarademono/impera; README clone/release links identify the latter as canonical. Promote the substantive enhanced upstream once, not both copies.
